title: Shock-guard materiality floor mixes a currency-agnostic absolute revenue jump against $-denominated floor without using the FX-converted basis, and the floor uses `|| 0` falsy fallback
evidence: `_materialityFloor`: `const ttm = (ttmRev && ttmRev[0]) || 0;` and `const mcap = ... (mcapField && mcapField.value) || 0;` then `Math.max(10000000, 0.08*ttm, 0.0025*mcap)`. The `|| 0` collapses a legitimate zero and any falsy envelope to 0, so the floor degrades to the flat $10M for any snapshot where ttmRev[0] or mcap is missing/zero — and the `jump = latest - med` (line 74) is compared against this floor (line 75). pull-yahoo.js:462-463 converts all series to USD and overwrites meta.reportingCurrency='USD', so the magnitudes are USD here — but the $10M hard floor is applied uniformly with no per-currency provenance check, so a snapshot that failed FX conversion (meta.fxConversionFailed, pull-yahoo.js:293/316 leaves values in local currency) gets a USD floor applied to non-USD magnitudes.
why_it_matters: revenue-shock-guard is a DATAGUARD (method-types.js:132) — a false shock disqualifies the stock universe-wide. The fxConversionFailed path (a few snapshots per pull per the pull-yahoo comments) means JPY/KRW magnitude jumps (hundreds of millions in local units) are compared against a $10M floor and will almost always exceed it, producing spurious REVENUE_SHOCK disqualifications on exactly the foreign issuers the FX path failed on.
fix: Skip the shock guard (return computable:false) when stock.meta.fxConversionFailed===true rather than evaluating magnitude tests on unconverted values; and replace `|| 0` with explicit Number.isFinite checks so a missing ttm/mcap yields incomputable, not a silently weakened floor. Comment: 'prevents USD floor applied to unconverted foreign magnitudes from manufacturing false shocks'.

_verdict.note:
Refuted on both sub-claims with source evidence.

FX/provenance claim is moot: snapshots with meta.fxConversionFailed===true never reach the scoring stage where revenue-shock-guard.js runs. In the full-pull path, pull-yahoo.js:1992-2001 detects fxConversionFailed after _convertSnapshotToUSD, logs '⊘ skipped: fx-unknown', fs.unlinkSync's any existing on-disk snapshot, pushes status 'fx-unknown', and returns BEFORE the snapshot is written. The price-only fast path (pull-yahoo.js:1560-1562) throws ('price-only refused: non-USD original with no fxRateApplied') for exactly that shape. So no unconverted-foreign-magnitude snapshot is ever persisted or scored. After successful conversion (pull-yahoo.js:446-468) all annual/quarterly/timeseries series and marketCap are scaled to USD and meta.reportingCurrency='USD' — so the $10M floor IS USD-denominated against USD magnitudes. The premise 'a snapshot that failed FX conversion gets a USD floor applied to non-USD magnitudes' cannot occur. The auditor even cites the skip behavior (pull-yahoo.js:287-288) but then assumes it doesn't fire.

The `|| 0` 'weakened floor' claim is backwards. _materialityFloor returns Math.max(10000000, 0.08*ttm, 0.0025*mcap) (line 36). $10M is the intended HARD MINIMUM; the scale-adaptive terms only RAISE it for large caps. The shock test is `jump > floor` (lines 75/95) — a lower floor makes the guard MORE sensitive (more likely to flag), not less. Collapsing a missing ttm/mcap to the $10M minimum is the conservative default, not a silent integrity failure. There is no scenario where this manufactures a false negative on a real shock.

Conclusion: not a real bug; based on a misread of where fxConversionFailed snapshots flow and an inverted reading of the Math.max floor semantics.

title: Materiality `ttRev / mcap >= 0.005` uses an already-FX-converted ttmRev but mcap can still be a raw envelope of 0; ratio path silently disabled for zero-mcap
evidence: `const isMaterial = ttmRev >= MATERIAL_REV_FLOOR || (mcap > 0 && ttmRev / mcap >= MATERIAL_MCAP_RATIO);` with `const mcap = (typeof mcapField === 'number') ? mcapField : (mcapField && mcapField.value) || 0;`. When mcap resolves to 0 (missing field), the ratio branch is skipped, so a sub-$100M-revenue micro-cap that WOULD be material by mcap-ratio is declared IMMATERIAL → pass-by-default (line 161-164), letting a genuine Q-spike micro-cap through the hard gate. The `|| 0` on mcap is the silent falsy trap.
why_it_matters: q-spike-dataguard is a DATAGUARD (method-types.js:133) gating the IONQ/quantum-spike pattern. A zero/missing mcap (common for fresh listings — the exact cohort prone to Q-spikes) flips the gate OFF, defeating the guard's purpose for its highest-risk population.
fix: When mcap is missing, fall back to the absolute revenue floor only and FLAG low-confidence rather than treating immateriality as pass; or source mcap from a secondary field. Replace `|| 0` with Number.isFinite guard and branch explicitly on 'mcap unknown'. Comment: 'prevents missing-mcap micro-caps from bypassing the Q-spike hard gate'.

_verdict.note:
FALSE POSITIVE — the alleged gate escape does not exist; it is caught by the partner method by design.

Trace (file: C:/Users/Karlr/screener-wt/audit-hardening/methods/q-spike-dataguard.js line 159, and methods/hypergrowth-quality-class.js):

1. Direction is inverted. The mcap-ratio branch `ttmRev/mcap >= 0.005` makes a stock MATERIAL when revenue is >=0.5% of mcap. Skipping it (mcap resolves to 0) makes the stock LESS likely to be material, i.e. routes it to IMMATERIAL — the conservative direction, not a bypass. The auditor's phrase "WOULD be material by mcap-ratio" is undefined when mcap is genuinely absent (no value to compute the ratio against).

2. The "pass-by-default lets a Q-spike micro-cap through the hard gate" premise is false. q-spike-dataguard returning pass=true/IMMATERIAL is a documented, deliberate hand-off (lines 15-17 and 162-163: "Mini-Stocks werden nicht hier gefiltert, sondern in hypergrowth-quality-class als LOW_BASE_EFFECT markiert"). The partner method methods/hypergrowth-quality-class.js uses the IDENTICAL materiality logic (line 70, same `(mcapField && mcapField.value) || 0`) and classifies ANY immaterial stock as LOW_BASE_EFFECT (lines 143-145 — the Bug #18 fix that made this fire regardless of growth rate). LOW_BASE_EFFECT has RANK 2 and `pass = value >= 4` (line 187), so hypergrowth-quality-class returns pass=false. The micro-cap is caught exactly as designed.

3. Missing-mcap is already a flagged upstream condition: data-quality.js lists marketCap as a required metric (weight 1.0), and strategy-modes.js lines 192-194 (Bug #22 fix) explicitly hard-fail missing mcap in mcap-floored modes. It is not a silent blind spot.

Residual minor point (does not make this a medium bug): `|| 0` would also collapse a legitimate marketCap.value===0 to 0, but a $0 market cap is not a real listed-equity condition, and the conservative LOW_BASE_EFFECT routing still applies, so no genuine Q-spike micro-cap escapes the overall gate.

fix_safe=false: the proposed fix (replace `|| 0` with Number.isFinite guard + new 'mcap unknown' branch + low-confidence flag) changes the result value/reason output, which drifts the fixture-hash invariant (see _helpers.js lines 155-175, tag28 pre-pull test gate), and would de-sync q-spike-dataguard from hypergrowth-quality-class which still uses `|| 0` — a worse, divergent state. Needs human review, not auto-apply.

title: Annual-fallback z-score uses a magic `99` sentinel when MAD==0 and ratio>5, but `5x` threshold and `99` are unexplained and bypass the materiality jump-check asymmetrically
evidence: `const z = (mad > 0) ? (y0 - med) / (1.4826 * mad) : (med > 0 && y0 / med > 5 ? 99 : 0);`. When prior annual revenues are identical (MAD==0, common for flat 3-year histories), any >5x jump is hard-coded to z=99, and then `shock = absZ > THRESHOLD && jump > floor` (line 95) — so it still requires jump>floor, but the 99 sentinel means there is no graduation: a 5.01x jump and a 50x jump are identical. Meanwhile the quarterly branch (line 72) sets z=0 when mad==0 with no equivalent ratio escape hatch, so the two code paths treat the same degenerate-MAD condition inconsistently.
why_it_matters: Inconsistent handling of the zero-dispersion case between quarterly and annual paths means the same underlying shock is caught annually but missed quarterly (or vice versa) depending only on which data tier is present. DATAGUARD verdicts should not depend on tier-specific magic numbers.
fix: Unify the MAD==0 handling across both branches: when dispersion is zero, fall back to a relative-jump ratio test with a single named constant (e.g. SHOCK_RATIO_WHEN_NO_DISPERSION) instead of a 99 sentinel in one branch and silent 0 in the other. Comment naming the failure mode: 'prevents tier-dependent shock detection when prior-period MAD is zero'.

_verdict.note:
Partially real but overstated. CONFIRMED inconsistency: the quarterly branch (revenue-shock-guard.js:72) maps MAD==0 to z=0 (never flags), while the annual branch (:92) maps MAD==0 + y0/med>5 to z=99 (flags). Same zero-dispersion condition, opposite outcomes — a genuine code smell.

REFUTED claims: (1) The title's core assertion that the 99 sentinel "bypasses the materiality jump-check asymmetrically" is FALSE. Line 95 `shock = absZ > THRESHOLD && jump > floor` applies the identical `jump > floor` materiality gate to the 99 path; the auditor's own evidence text concedes this ("it still requires jump>floor"), contradicting the title. (2) "No graduation: 5.01x and 50x identical" is technically true but a non-issue: revenue-shock-guard is consumed ONLY as a binary signal. It is a soft-guard (score-aggregator.js:202, fixed 7-pt SOFT_GUARD_PENALTY) in HYPERGROWTH/QUALITY (strategy-modes.js:92) and a data-guard in TURNAROUND (:160). Both consumers read only `r.pass === false` (strategy-modes.js:206 and :219). It is NOT in the graduated SCORE_WEIGHTS path, so the magnitude of value/absZ (99 vs a real z) never affects any score. Graduating the z would change zero downstream behavior.

Net: this is a code-quality/consistency smell, not a correctness bug — no wrong screener output results. If anything the annual branch is the more-protective (more correct) one and the quarterly mad==0→0 is the under-protective gap. Severity medium → low.

fix_safe=false: the proposed unification would make the quarterly branch also flag flat-base >5x jumps — a real behavior change that flips currently-passing stocks to flagged and alters value/absZ outputs. The repo gates on a golden snapshot (tests/fixture-hash.txt, consumed by generate-screener.js and engine-cli-tests.js); any change to z-computation risks shifting the fixture hash / breaking CI and changes live screening results. Needs human review + fixture re-baseline. The cosmetic part (rename 99 to a named constant + comment) is safe, but the auditor's actual proposed_fix (unify the two branches' MAD==0 handling) is not.

title: Materiality re-applies FX conversion using meta.reportingCurrency, which pull-yahoo overwrites to 'USD' AFTER converting values — for fxConversionFailed snapshots the values are local-ccy but currency reads 'USD', disabling the floor incorrectly
evidence: `const reportingCurrency = (stock.meta && stock.meta.reportingCurrency) || 'USD'; const ttmRevUsd = toUsdRough(ttmRev, reportingCurrency);`. pull-yahoo.js:462-463 sets `meta.reportingCurrency='USD'` for every successfully converted snapshot (values already USD → toUsdRough multiplies by 1.0, correct). BUT for fxConversionFailed snapshots (pull-yahoo.js:293, 316: values left in local ccy, fxConverted:false) meta.reportingCurrency is also left such that the guard cannot tell converted from unconverted — it trusts the tag and applies rate 1.0 to local-currency magnitudes. A JPY reporter (¥ in the hundreds of billions) then trivially clears the $100M USD floor and is subjected to the -25% decline test on raw yen YoY (ratios are unit-free so that part survives), but the materiality classification is wrong-by-luck rather than correct-by-design.
why_it_matters: The FX-mismatch class is exactly what pull-yahoo.js:271-274 calls out as 'silently corrupting every ratio for non-USD stocks'. This guard re-introduces a softer version of it: it cannot distinguish 'already USD' from 'conversion failed, still local' because both surface as reportingCurrency without a converted-flag check.
fix: Read stock.meta.fxConverted / fxConversionFailed and stock.meta.reportingCurrencyOriginal instead of the post-conversion reportingCurrency; treat fxConversionFailed snapshots as incomputable for the USD-denominated materiality test. Comment: 'prevents post-conversion USD tag from masking unconverted local-ccy magnitudes in the materiality floor'.

_verdict.note:
False positive on two independent grounds, both verified in C:/Users/Karlr/screener-wt/audit-hardening.

(1) The premise is inverted. The auditor claims fxConversionFailed snapshots have values in local ccy but meta.reportingCurrency reading 'USD'. The code does the opposite. In _convertSnapshotToUSD (pull-yahoo.js), only the SUCCESSFUL conversion path sets snap.meta.reportingCurrency='USD' (line 463). The failure paths do NOT touch reportingCurrency: the unknown-currency branch (lines 311-318) sets reportingCurrencyOriginal=origCurrency, fxConversionFailed=true, fxConverted=false but leaves reportingCurrency at its original non-USD value; the OTC-ambiguous branch (lines 290-296) only fires when origCurrency==='USD' anyway. So the guard at revenue-volatility-guard.js:78 reads the ORIGINAL currency for a failed snapshot, not 'USD'. For the auditor's JPY example, toUsdRough(ttmRev,'JPY') would apply the 0.0067 rate correctly — not rate 1.0. (Also JPY is in FX_TO_USD, so it would not be a conversion failure at all; a real failure needs a currency missing from the table, in which case toUsdRough returns the value unchanged via line 58, the documented conservative behavior.)

(2) Even granting the premise, fxConversionFailed snapshots never reach the guard. pull-yahoo.js:1992-2001: after _convertSnapshotToUSD, the pull loop hard-skips any snapshot with meta.fxConversionFailed===true — logs 'fx-unknown', deletes the stale snapshot file (fs.unlinkSync), pushes status:'fx-unknown', and returns BEFORE persisting/scoring. The volatility guard only runs against persisted snapshots during scoring, so it can never see an fxConversionFailed snapshot. The described corruption is structurally unreachable.

The proposed fix targets an unreachable state and is based on a misread of where reportingCurrency='USD' is assigned.

_verdict.note:
The headline claim (category=dead-code: "never evaluated in the default path", "only runs when a caller explicitly opts it in — which nothing does") is REFUTED by the runner. In methods/runner.js the canonical export `evaluateStock` is `evaluateStockLegacy` (line 83-90), which calls the internal `evaluateStock(stock)` with NO opts, so `onlyDefault` is false (line 45). Grep across the whole worktree for `onlyDefault` shows exactly one caller passing the option, and it passes `{ onlyDefault: false }` (scripts/regional-oos-test.js:43); NO caller anywhere passes true. The production entry point generate-screener.js:259, all backtests, reports and methods-cli all call `Runner.evaluateStock(stock)` with no opts. Carrying no SCORE_WEIGHTS/softGuard entry is the documented DIAGNOSTIC design (method-types.js:54), identical to ~20 other defaultActive:false DIAGNOSTIC methods (margin-decay, capex-trend, opinc-margin-spike, etc.) — it surfaces in per-method detail output, it is not dead.

The SECONDARY subpoint is real but is a different, lower-severity finding: line 24 `.filter(v => v != null && v > 0)` then indexes values[0..3] as calendar-contiguous quarters (lines 33-37). Severity low, not medium, and it is not the dead-code finding that was filed.
